title: Technology Sector Update for 10/18/2018: MDSO,TSM,ERIC,SAP
text:

Technology stocks were retreating in recent trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 ( XLK ) losing almost 1.8% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (^SOX) was falling nearly 2.4%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Medidata Solutions ( MDSO ) was almost 4% higher in late Thursday trading, rebounding from a slim decline soon after the opening bell despite the software-as-a-service company reporting improved Q3 financial results and also exceeding analyst estimates. Excluding one-time items, Medidata earned $0.42 per share, up from $0.34 during the same quarter last year and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.06 per share. Revenue rose to $163.4 million from $138.9 million last year to also top the $162.1 million Street view.
In other sector news:
(+) Ericsson ( ERIC ) stretched out its early Thursday gains, rising just over 6%, after the mobile communications equipment company reported non-GAAP Q3 net income of SEK1.03, or about $0.11, per share, reversing a SEK0.29 per share net loss during the same quarter last year. Total sales rose to SEK53.8 billion from SEK49.4 billion last year.
(-) Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM ) has continued to lose ground on Thursday, falling almost 3% after giving back a 1% advance that followed the chipmaker reporting a 3.3% increase in its Q3 revenue to NT$260.35 billion, or about $8.41 billion, and exceeding Wall Street projections looking for NT$257.80 billion in revenue. Net income slipped 0.9% year-over-year to NT$3.44 per share, or $0.56 per American depositary share, also squeaking past the NT$3.43 per share analyst mean.
(-) SAP ( SAP ) dropped more than 7% on Thursday despite boosting its FY18 outlook following a big jump in Q3 revenue compared with year-ago levels, supported by growth in its cloud and software offerings. Revenue rose 8% year-over-year during the July-to-September reporting period to EUR6.02 billion, or about $6.94 billion. Pre-tax profit declined 2% to EUR947 million from EUR993 million euros during the year-ago quarter while its operating profit slipped 5.6% to EUR1.24 billion from EUR1.31 billion last year.
